lines.trans: Vitya, tell me, what happened to you?
It seems I just accidentally sprained my ankle.
My God, well that is it, you urgently need to see a doctor!
So for today we are done with golf.
No, I want very much to finish playing this round.
Right now I will go rest a little and return to you.
Viktor Petrovich, are you definitely sure about that?
In general, golf is the best thing I have played in my life!
Why walk on foot, they will give you a quick ride right now.
Lena, do not be bored here, I will be back soon!
Hey, what am I paying you money for, quickly switch it to football!
Guys, attention, today I am quitting and leaving for another restaurant.
Congratulations, just do not forget to buy us some good juice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'say', paired with 'говорить'.

meanings.en: to finish, to end, to complete
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'кончить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to finish, to complete', paired with 'заканчивать'.

examples.text: Давайте лучше играть, можно я сейчас ударю?
examples.trans: Let us play instead, may I take a shot right now?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'played', paired with 'сыграть'.

examples.text: Сегодня наш любимый клуб «Спартак» играет.
examples.trans: Today our favorite club Spartak is playing.

examples.text: Это смотря как наша игра закончится.
examples.trans: That depends on how our game ends.

examples.text: Дима, наши сегодня выиграли!
examples.trans: Dima, our team won today!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я же дал своё честное слово.
examples.trans: After all, I gave my honest word.

examples.text: Иду против всех своих принципов.
examples.trans: I am going against all my principles.

examples.text: Вообще гольф — это лучшее, во что я играл в свою жизнь!
examples.trans: In general, golf is the best thing I have played in my life!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, что у нас есть целая жизнь.
examples.trans: I hope that we have a whole life.

examples.text: У нас есть целая жизнь.
examples.trans: We have a whole life.

examples.text: Вообще гольф — это лучшее, во что я играл в свою жизнь!
examples.trans: In general, golf is the best thing I have played in my life!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'why', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Макс, а зачем ты это сейчас надел?
examples.trans: Max, why did you put that on right now?

examples.text: Зачем идти пешком, вас сейчас быстро подвезут.
examples.trans: Why walk on foot, they will give you a quick ride right now.

examples.text: Зачем ты пришёл?
examples.trans: What have you come for?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Витя, можешь идти куда хочешь.
examples.trans: Vitya, you can go wherever you want.

examples.text: Зачем идти пешком, вас сейчас быстро подвезут.
examples.trans: Why walk on foot, they will give you a quick ride right now.

examples.text: Я иду домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'on foot', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Зачем идти пешком, вас сейчас быстро подвезут.
examples.trans: Why walk on foot, they will give you a quick ride right now.

examples.text: Давай дальше ты пойдёшь пешком.
examples.trans: Let us have you walk the rest on foot.

examples.text: Давай отсюда ты дойдёшь пешком.
examples.trans: Let's have you walk from here.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Максим, ну-ка быстро иди сюда.
examples.trans: Maxim, come over here quickly.

examples.text: Конечно, можешь, только давай быстро.
examples.trans: Of course you may, just make it quick.

examples.text: Ещё и быстрый рост у тебя намечается.
examples.trans: And rapid growth is on the horizon for you too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'везти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will give a ride'.

related.gloss: to will give a ride (base verb)
not to will give a ride (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Зачем идти пешком, вас сейчас быстро подвезут.
examples.trans: Why walk on foot, they will give you a quick ride right now.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и подвезти вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will give a ride on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Витя, а я тут хорошо подумал.
examples.trans: Vitya, I have thought it over well here.

examples.text: Лена, ты тут не скучай, я скоро буду!
examples.trans: Lena, do not be bored here, I will be back soon!

examples.text: Лена, ну извини, я иду, а тут наш футбол.
examples.trans: Lena, well forgive me, I was walking and here was our football.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если, конечно, футбол тебе дороже, чем я.
examples.trans: If, of course, football is dearer to you than I am.

examples.text: Сказал, что его блюда едят только в ресторане.
examples.trans: He said that his dishes are eaten only in the restaurant.

examples.text: Вот как с ним бороться, я не понимаю.
examples.trans: How to deal with him, I do not understand.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'кучать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be bored / miss', paired with 'соскучиться'.

examples.text: Дорогая, чего-то я уже скучать начал.
examples.trans: Darling, for some reason I already started missing you.

examples.text: О, привет, молодец, что зашёл, мы прямо скучали!
examples.trans: Oh, hi, good job dropping by, we really missed you!

examples.text: Лена, ты тут не скучай, я скоро буду!
examples.trans: Lena, do not be bored here, I will be back soon!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Давай выпьем хорошего шампанского.
examples.trans: Let us drink some good champagne.

examples.text: Принеси нам шампанского, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Bring us some champagne, please.

examples.text: Наши выиграли, давай скорее наливай!
examples.trans: Our team won, come on, pour quickly!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.text: Или ты не хочешь быть уборщиком?
examples.trans: Or do you not want to be a cleaner?

examples.text: Я хотел быть похожим на вас, а сейчас понял, что лучше Воронеж, чем с вами на одной кухне!
examples.trans: I wanted to be like you, and now I understood that Voronezh is better than being in the same kitchen with you!

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hey', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Эй, я тебе за что деньги плачу, быстро на футбол переключил!
examples.trans: Hey, what am I paying you money for, quickly switch it to football!

examples.text: Эй, ты что?
examples.trans: Hey, what's wrong?

examples.text: Эй, иди сюда!
examples.trans: Hey, come here!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сказал, что его блюда едят только в ресторане.
examples.trans: He said that his dishes are eaten only in the restaurant.

examples.text: Мы же с тобой в кино ходили три раза.
examples.trans: After all, you and I went to the movies three times.

examples.text: А я часа через два к тебе заеду.
examples.trans: And I will drop by your place in about two hours.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Если деньги будешь просить, не дам.
examples.trans: If you are going to ask for money, I will not give any.

examples.text: Эй, я тебе за что деньги плачу, быстро на футбол переключил!
examples.trans: Hey, what am I paying you money for, quickly switch it to football!

examples.text: У меня нет денег.
examples.trans: I have no money.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'pay', paired with 'заплатить'.

examples.text: Мы хорошо платим.
examples.trans: We pay well.

examples.text: Кто платит?
examples.trans: Who is paying?

examples.text: А вашу работу вернуть можно. И мы хорошо платим.
examples.trans: But we can get your job back for you. And we pay well.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'football' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Если, конечно, футбол тебе дороже, чем я.
examples.trans: If, of course, football is dearer to you than I am.

examples.text: Эй, я тебе за что деньги плачу, быстро на футбол переключил!
examples.trans: Hey, what am I paying you money for, quickly switch it to football!

examples.text: Лена, ну извини, я иду, а тут наш футбол.
examples.trans: Lena, well forgive me, I was walking and here was our football.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'ключить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'switched'.

examples.text: Эй, я тебе за что деньги плачу, быстро на футбол переключил!
examples.trans: Hey, what am I paying you money for, quickly switch it to football!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и переключить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and switched on time.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'guys, team' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ребята, скажите, как поживает ваш орёл?
examples.trans: Guys, tell us, how is your Eagle doing?

examples.text: Ребята, внимание, я сегодня увольняюсь и ухожу в другой ресторан.
examples.trans: Guys, attention, today I am quitting and leaving for another restaurant.

examples.text: Ребята, давайте выпьем за моего коллегу Максима!
examples.trans: Guys, let us drink to my colleague Maxim!

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Не обращайте внимания, это Виктор Петрович шутит.
examples.trans: Pay no attention, Viktor Petrovich is joking.

examples.text: Ребята, внимание, я сегодня увольняюсь и ухожу в другой ресторан.
examples.trans: Guys, attention, today I am quitting and leaving for another restaurant.

examples.text: Прошу внимания.
examples.trans: May I have your attention.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'вольняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am quitting / resigning'.

examples.text: А я пока увольняюсь.
examples.trans: And I am quitting in the meantime.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и увольняться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and am quitting on time.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'leave', paired with 'уйти'.

examples.text: Никуда не уходи, я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Do not go anywhere, I will be back soon.

examples.text: Ну, если уходишь, тогда получи свой расчёт!
examples.trans: Well, if you are leaving, then get your final settlement!

examples.text: Я ухожу домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('another').

examples.text: Нет, я просто к подруге в гости пришла.
examples.trans: No, I just came to visit a friend.

examples.text: Ребята, внимание, я сегодня увольняюсь и ухожу в другой ресторан.
examples.trans: Guys, attention, today I am quitting and leaving for another restaurant.

examples.text: Ладно, всё равно это очень круто, мой друг!
examples.trans: Alright, it is still very cool, my friend!

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Сказал, что его блюда едят только в ресторане.
examples.trans: He said that his dishes are eaten only in the restaurant.

examples.text: Я выкупил вторую половину ресторана у Кристины.
examples.trans: I bought out the second half of the restaurant from Kristina.

examples.text: А мне уже предложили место в новом ресторане.
examples.trans: They already offered me a position at a new restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здравлять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'congratulations', paired with 'поздравить'.

examples.text: Поздравляю, только не забудь купить нам хороший сок.
examples.trans: Congratulations, just do not forget to buy us some good juice.

examples.text: Здорово, поздравляю!
examples.trans: Great, congratulations!

examples.text: Поздравляю тебя с праздником!
examples.trans: Happy holiday to you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сказал, что его блюда едят только в ресторане.
examples.trans: He said that his dishes are eaten only in the restaurant.

examples.text: Я ведь Макса возвращаю только ради тебя, Дима.
examples.trans: After all, I am bringing Max back only for your sake, Dima.

examples.text: А он только в телевизоре смешно выглядит.
examples.trans: And he only looks funny on television.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.text: Не забудь помыть унитаз.
examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Я забыл ключи.
examples.trans: I forgot the keys.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Я выкупил вторую половину ресторана у Кристины.
examples.trans: I bought out the second half of the restaurant from Kristina.

examples.text: Поздравляю, только не забудь купить нам хороший сок.
examples.trans: Congratulations, just do not forget to buy us some good juice.

examples.text: Я купил герметик.
examples.trans: I've bought sealant.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.text: Хорошо, милая, как скажешь, так и будет.
examples.trans: Alright, darling, as you say, so it will be.

examples.text: Давай выпьем хорошего шампанского.
examples.trans: Let us drink some good champagne.

examples.text: Шеф, вы сегодня очень хорошо выглядите.
examples.trans: Chef, you look very good today.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'juice' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Поздравляю, только не забудь купить нам хороший сок.
examples.trans: Congratulations, just do not forget to buy us some good juice.

examples.text: Апельсиновый сок.
examples.trans: Orange juice.

examples.text: Я выпью немного хорошего сока.
examples.trans: I will drink a little good juice.
